en: Revenue lost by no-show rate and appointments
Type the appointments a month, the no-show rate, the price and the deposit kept for each no-show; the grid tries other rates and volumes so you see how fast the loss grows.
Extra revenue lost above your target rate
No-show rate against appointments a month
Client: a reminder for your appointment
Hello {client}, a reminder of your {service} on {date} at {start} with {technician}. Please reply to confirm.
Hello {client}, please confirm your {service} on {date} at {start}. Reply to keep it, or tell us if you need to move it.
Client: deposit to hold your slot
Hello {client}, a deposit of {deposit} holds your {service} on {date}. Please pay it so we can keep your slot.
Hello {client}, your deposit of {amount} for the appointment on {date} has been received. Thank you.
Hello {client}, we missed you on {date}. Can we find you a new time for your {service}?
Hello {client}, your cancellation on {date} was inside the notice time, so {fee_kept} of your deposit is kept. Please reply with any question.
Hello {offered_to}, a slot opened on {date} at {start} for {service}, about {minutes_free} minutes. Would you like it?
Client: a waiting list slot opened
Hello {client}, a slot for your {service} has opened. Please reply today if you want it.
Hello {client}, your appointment on {date} is now at {new_start}. Sorry for the change, please reply to confirm.
Client: running late, please let us know
Hello {client}, your {service} with {technician} is at {start} on {date}. If you are running late please let us know and we will hold the slot for a short time.
Hello {client}, {technician} is away on {date}. We can offer new times for your {service}. Please reply with the days that suit you.
Client: thank you for the early notice
Hello {client}, thank you for telling us early about {date}. We have new times for your {service} when you are ready.
Hello, your day on {date} has {booked_minutes} booked minutes against {bookable_minutes} bookable. Please check it with the front desk.
Technician: free time, open for walk-ins
Hello, you have {free_minutes} free minutes on {date}. The day is open for walk-ins.
Technician: a client moved to you
Hello, {client} moved to your column on {date} at {new_start} for {service}.
Hello, your book for {date} is ready: {appointments} appointments and {booked_minutes} booked minutes.
Technician: please confirm your days off
Hello, please confirm your time off from {from_date} to {to_date}. {clients_to_move} clients need new times.
Technician: a no-show, your slot is open
Hello, {client} did not come on {date}. Your slot for {service} is open.
Hello, please confirm the appointments of {technician} on {date}: {appointments} are in the book.
Front desk: call the waiting list
Hello, please call {client} on the waiting list for {service}, wanted by {wanted_by}.
Hello, the deposit of {amount} for {client} (appointment {appointment_id}) on {date} is not paid yet. Please chase it.
Front desk: a technician is overbooked
Hello, {technician} is overbooked on {date} by {minutes_over} minutes. Please move {to_move} appointments.
Front desk: fill the open slots
Hello, {technician} has {minutes_free} free minutes on {date} at {start}. Please offer the slot.
Hello, no-shows in the month of {month} are {no_shows}, a rate of {no_show_rate}. Check the reminders and the deposits.
Hello, {technician} is overbooked on {date}: {booked_minutes} minutes booked, {minutes_over} over.
Hello, utilisation of {technician} on {date} is {utilisation}, below the wanted level. {free_minutes} minutes are free.
Hello, deposit {deposit_id} of {amount} is held for {client} for the appointment on {date}. Days held: {days_held}.
Owner: the capacity forecast is ready
Hello, the capacity forecast is ready: on {date} {technician} has {free_minutes} free minutes. Open the forecast sheet for the next 14 days.
Daily appointment sheet of {set:company}, dated {today}. Day {col:techdays.day_id}: {col:techdays.date}. Technician: {col:techdays.technician}, {col:techdays.resource}.

Appointments in the book: {col:techdays.appointments}. Booked minutes with set-up: {col:techdays.booked_minutes} of {col:techdays.bookable_minutes} bookable. Utilisation (the share of bookable minutes that are sold): {col:techdays.utilisation}.
Free minutes: {col:techdays.free_minutes}. Minutes over capacity: {col:techdays.over_minutes}. Day check: {col:techdays.day_flag}.
Print this sheet before the first client, tick each appointment as it is done and write any change on the Same-Day Changes sheet. Technician phone: {col:techdays.tech_phone}.
Weekly book summary for one technician

Weekly book of {set:company}, dated {today}. Team member {col:team.staff_id}: {col:team.name}, {col:team.role}, {col:team.pay_model}. Chair or room: {col:team.resource}. Hours a week: {col:team.hours_week}.
Booked minutes in the next 14 days: {col:team.booked_14}. Utilisation of the last 30 days: {col:team.util_30}. Days over capacity in the next 14 days: {col:team.days_over_14}.
Agree the week with the front desk and write any day off on the Time Off sheet.
Appointment confirmation of {set:company}, dated {today}. Appointment {col:appointments.appointment_id} for {col:appointments.client}.

Service: {col:appointments.service}, {col:appointments.minutes} minutes, with {col:appointments.technician} at {col:appointments.resource}. Date {col:appointments.date}, from {col:appointments.start} to {col:appointments.end}.
Price {col:appointments.list_price}, before any tax. A deposit of {col:appointments.deposit} holds the slot for services of {set:deposit_from} and over.

Please give at least {set:cancel_notice_hours} hours of notice to move or cancel. Arrive a few minutes early and tell us about any allergy. Booking rules are sample wording, check your own local rules.
Deposit receipt of {set:company}, dated {today}. Deposit {col:deposits.deposit_id} for appointment {col:deposits.appointment_id} on {col:deposits.date}.

Client: {col:deposits.client}. Technician: {col:deposits.technician}. Deposit: {col:deposits.amount}. Asked for on {col:deposits.requested_on}. State: {col:deposits.state}. Deposit check: {col:deposits.deposit_flag}.

The deposit counts toward the price of the service. If the appointment is cancelled inside the notice time, part or all of the deposit may be kept as the booking rules say. Refund so far: {col:deposits.refund_amount}.
Keep this receipt with the booking. Check your own local rules on deposits.
Cancellation or no-show notice to a client
Notice of {set:company}, dated {today}, for {col:noshows.client}. Appointment {col:noshows.appointment_id} on {col:noshows.date} with {col:noshows.technician} for {col:noshows.service}.
Status of the appointment: {col:noshows.status}. Price of the service: {col:noshows.price}. Deposit held: {col:noshows.deposit}. Fee kept under the booking rules: {col:noshows.fee_kept}.
A late cancel is a cancellation inside the notice time and a no-show is a client who does not come and does not cancel. Deposit check: {col:noshows.loss_flag}.
We would be glad to book a new time. Please call the front desk. The notice time is {set:cancel_notice_hours} hours.
Waiting list request summary for one client
Waiting list summary of {set:company}, dated {today}. Request {col:waiting.wait_id} from {col:waiting.client}, phone {col:waiting.client_phone}.

Service wanted: {col:waiting.service}, with {col:waiting.technician}. Requested on {col:waiting.requested_on}, wanted by {col:waiting.wanted_by}. Status: {col:waiting.status}. Days waiting: {col:waiting.days_waiting}.
An offer should go out within {set:wait_offer_days} days of the request. Record the answer on the Waiting List sheet.
Chair capacity report for one technician and weekday
Chair capacity report of {set:company}, dated {today}. Row {col:weekday.row_id}: {col:weekday.technician} on {col:weekday.weekday}, last 12 weeks.

Completed appointments: {col:weekday.appointments}. Booked minutes with set-up: {col:weekday.booked_minutes} of {col:weekday.bookable_minutes} bookable. Utilisation: {col:weekday.utilisation}, the wanted level is {set:target_utilisation}.
Free minutes: {col:weekday.free_minutes}. Appointments per working day: {col:weekday.per_day}. Check: {col:weekday.util_flag}.
Use the free minutes to plan offers for quiet days and to move clients from days that are too full.
No-show review of {set:company}, dated {today}, for the month starting {col:months.month}. Row {col:months.month_id}.
Value lost: {col:months.lost_value}. Revenue: {col:months.revenue}, {col:months.rev_per_appt} per appointment. No-show check: {col:months.rate_flag}.
The no-show target is {set:target_noshow}. Compare the month with the Reminder Schedule and the booking rules.
Booking and cancellation policy for one rule
Booking and cancellation policy of {set:company}, dated {today}. Rule: {col:rules.rule}. Applies to: {col:rules.applies_to}.

Notice needed: {col:rules.notice_hours} hours ({col:rules.notice_days} days). Share of the deposit kept: {col:rules.fee_pct}, which is {col:rules.fee_on_deposit} on a standard deposit. Fee check: {col:rules.fee_flag}.
This wording is a sample. Adapt it to your own practice and check your own local rules before you show it to clients.

Open slot offer of {set:company}, dated {today}. Slot {col:openslots.slot_id}: {col:openslots.date} at {col:openslots.start}, {col:openslots.minutes_free} free minutes with {col:openslots.technician}.
Service offered: {col:openslots.service}. Offered to: {col:openslots.offered_to}, phone {col:openslots.client_phone}. Status: {col:openslots.status}. Slot check: {col:openslots.slot_flag}.
Value if filled: {col:openslots.filled_value}. Days to the slot: {col:openslots.days_to}.
Offer the slot to the waiting list first and write the answer on the Open Slots sheet.

Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: bookable minutes a day, set-up time, wanted utilisation, notice hours, deposit and the no-show target.
Check Team, Resources, Services and Working Days. They hold the people, the chairs, the services with minutes, price and deposit and the days each technician works.

Enter each appointment on Appointments with its date, times, technician, chair, service, client, source, status and deposit. The end check, the lead time bucket and the phone numbers calculate themselves.

Keep Technician Days up to date with the appointments, booked minutes and bookable minutes of each day. Utilisation, free minutes and the over capacity flag show where to sell more and where to move a client.
Log every no-show and late cancel on No-show and Late Cancel Log and every deposit on Deposits, with its state: asked for, held, used, kept or refunded.
Use Waiting List, Open Slots and Same-Day Changes to fill free time and to record what changed on the day. Overbooking Checks and Time Off keep the book safe.
Read Reminder Schedule and Booking Rules for the reminders and the notice and fee rules you follow. Check your own local rules before you charge a fee.
Weekday Pattern, Time-of-Day Demand, Booking Sources, Month Summary and Seasons show when the studio is busy and when it is quiet.
Use the 14 calculators to check a day, find a slot, test a reminder, plan a day, price a no-show and forecast the next 14 days.
Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in.
Read the Appointment Dashboard and Charts every week: appointments, utilisation, no-shows, deposits, open slots filled and the technician days over capacity.

Client records with patch test, consent and readiness
One row per client: contact, visits, allergy note, patch test and consent form with dates; the tier, the patch test and consent states and the readiness for the next visit fill in.
Appointments with the patch test and consent flag
One row per appointment with service, client, status, price and tip; the patch test and consent status of the client and the readiness flag for an upcoming visit fill in.
Patch test status of the client
Consent form status of the client
Patch tests, consent forms and allergy reviews
One row per patch test (a small test of a product on a small area of skin), consent form or allergy review; the client id, the days left and the state fill in by themselves.
Before and after photo log with consent to share
One row per before and after photo kept as text: the client, the service, the technician, the photo reference and whether the client agreed to share it; the share state fills in.
Patch tests needed before an upcoming visit
One row per upcoming visit that needs a valid patch test: the visit date, the patch test date on file and the technician; the days to the visit and the ready flag fill in by themselves.
Allergy notes as the client gave them
One row per client with an allergy noted by the client: the note, the products to avoid, the date and who noted it; the patch test status and the review flag fill in. Never a diagnosis.
Client preferences for quiet visits, drinks and contact
One row per client with a preference: preferred technician, contact channel, quiet visit, drink and notes; the allergy note, the patch test and the technician phone fill in by themselves.
One row per note about a client: the date, the note, who wrote it and whether a follow-up is needed; the days old, the follow-up flag and the visits of the client fill in by themselves.
Consent forms that run out soon
One row per consent form close to its end: the date signed, the date it expires and the technician; the days left and the state fill in. Check your own local rules on how long a form stays valid.
Client segments with the clients in each
The five client tiers with the rule that puts a client in each; the number of clients in each tier fills in from the Clients sheet.
Services with minutes, price, deposit and patch test need
One row per service: minutes, price, deposit and whether a patch test is needed first; the clients whose main service it is and the photos kept fill in by themselves.
Team and outside contacts with studio figures
The owner, technicians, front desk and outside contacts (a booth renter is a technician who rents a chair and keeps their own takings); the studio figures used in owner messages fill in.
First visits in 14 days not ready
The six booking channels with the clients each one brought; the share of all clients fills in by itself.
Birthday offers with use and days left
One row per birthday offer sent: the client, the offer, the discount and when it was used; the valid until date, the days to use and the state fill in by themselves.
First visits with the readiness flag
One row per first visit of a new client: the service, the deposit paid, the patch test and the consent form; the deposit due, the days to the visit and the ready flag fill in by themselves.
New and returning clients by month
One row per month from the appointment book: new clients, returning clients, completed appointments and revenue; the new client share and the average ticket fill in by themselves.
Redo requests with the outcome and days to resolve
One row per redo or fix request: the service, the technician, the issue, the outcome and the day it was or will be fixed; the days to resolve and the state fill in by themselves.
Client data requests with due date and days open
One row per request from a client about their record: the request, the status, the due date and when it was closed; the days open and the state fill in. Check your own local rules on how to answer.
One row per tag on a client: the tag, when it was added and by whom; the visits and the tier of the client fill in by themselves.
One row per pair of records that may be the same client: the second id, the reason, the check date and whether the records were merged or kept apart; the first id, the state and the phone fill in.
